items.title: 61539_Butter Jackson oral history interview
items.q: I left the band in Europe to go with Quincy Jones because we had a show called Free and Easy

ctx.x: So when I left the band, I didn't leave the band on account of because I didn't like the band. I left the band because I was tired of traveling and I left the band in Europe to go with Quincy Jones because we had a show called Free and Easy and Sammy Davis was supposed to be the star of the show had we had our full run in Europe and come back to the United States. And I knew that if Sammy Davis was going to be the star of the show, I would be in New York for a year, two

items.title: Quincy Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Clark Terry just left Duke Ellington. Quentin Jackson just left Duke Ellington. Phil Woods.

ctx.x: But you tell me all this stuff is an accident.

. . . I owed so much money when I came back, because when I had that band over there, I was 26. I had 33 people, dogs, Charlie Parker’s ex-wife, Charlie Parker’s son Baird, Phil Woods, dogs, grandmothers, everything. I – they told us when the show closed, you’ll get – on a Thursday – you’re guaranteed transportation to Saturday. I said, “I ain’t thinking about it. We’ve got a gig at the Olympic Theatre Saturday night.” Now that’s really logical, right? And one in Sweden. So I stayed over there with 33 people for…
How are they going to get home? They believed in you.
